newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samsung counters automakers' demand for apology.
newsitem.headline: Samsung counters automakers' demand for apology.

text.p: Samsung Motors Inc, a unit of South Korea's Samsung Group, said on Tuesday it had no plan to apologise over a dispute on the restructuring of the auto industry until prosecutors complete their probe.
"We are concerned about the real motives behind the pressure for an apology," said a Samsung spokesman said.

Earlier on Tuesday, Hyundai Motor Co and five other South Korean automakers repeated their demand that Samsung publicly apologise for asserting in a report that there was a "managerial conflict" at Kia Motors Corp.
"We don't want unnecessary discussion until the prosecution office comes up with the results of its investigation," the Samsung spokesman said.
"If we turn out to be innocent, the party that has caused the current problems should take all the responsibility," he said. He declined to elaborate.
Earlier this month, Kia Motors said Samsung argued in an internal report that Kia faced managerial conflicts and that Kia had reached its maximum growth potential.
Samsung said the report was an opinion by an individual employee and did not represent the company's official position.
Last Monday, Samsung Motors said it was not interested in any merger and acquisition deals and had no plan to seek any because it was already busy enough with its scheduled projects.
But analysts said a Samsung takeover of Kia, if realised, would give Samsung all it needed -- capacity, technology and, more importantly, a network of parts suppliers.

In 1994 Samsung won a government license to enter the car industry in a technical tie-up with Nissan. Samsung plans to make 80,000 vehicles in 1998, with the output rising to 250,000 in 1999 and 500,000 by 2002.
